Note that since $N \subseteq M$, we always have $\mathcal{G}(N) \subseteq \mathcal{G}(M)$. The condition $\mathcal{G}(N) = \mathcal{G}(M)$ means $N$ generates the entire group associated with $M$.
*   **BFM (Bounded Factorization Monoid)**: A monoid where the set of lengths of factorizations of any element is finite (though the number of factorizations can be infinite, the lengths are bounded). Every FFM is a BFM, but the converse is not always true.
